newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh refugees return home to warm welcome.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh refugees return home to warm welcome.

text.p: Bangladesh on Friday accorded a warm reception to tribal refugees returning home from India, and officials from the two countries heralded a new era in bilateral relations.
"This is the start of a new phase in our relationship," said Bangladesh government leader Abul Hasanat Abdullah.
Abdullah headed a team of senior civil and security officials who greeted the first batch of refugees as they walked over a bridge spanning the Feni river border into Bangladesh's Ramgarh township.
The refugees came from one of seven camps in Kathalchhari, a village in northeast India's Tripura state, across the river.

"I greet you," said Abdullah, parliamentary chief whip of the ruling Awami League. "It's your home and it's painful that you have lived in another country for so long. Today is a happy and memorable day for all of us."
Up to 50,000 tribespeople fled the Chittagong Hill Tracts to escape a 24-year revolt by Shanti Bahini guerrillas and a series of attacks on local tribes by Bengali-speaking settlers.
The Shanti Bahini want autonomy for the 5,500 square-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, which borders India and Burma. They also want some 300,000 settlers expelled from the region.
More than 8,500 civilians, rebels and government troops have been killed in the insurgency, according to official figures.
Officials said 278 refugees from 64 families were due to return on Friday. A total of 6,700 are expected to return to Bangladesh by April 7.
"It's a happy day for us, too," Upendralal Chakma, chief of the Tribal Refugees Association, said before the repatriation started.
"We believed the government in Dhaka would keep its pledge for proper rehabilitation of refugees," he told reporters at Kathalchhari in Tripura.
Friday's ceremony at the border crossing also was attended by Tripura Deputy Chief Minister Baidyanath Majumdar.
"I wish the refugees a happy and peaceful return to Bangladesh. After the water treaty, this is another milestone in our historic cooperation," the chief minister said.
Bangladesh and India last December signed a landmark treaty that spelled an end to decades of enmity between them over sharing of water from the Ganges river.
Officials said the second phase of the repatriation would begin one month after April 7 so refugee leaders could visit the Hill Tracts to see if the rehabilitation was satisfactory.
